rows.question: can an operator see whether collectors are running and what they return?
rows.note: scan volume, duration and the live-monitor fleet are emitted by the API
rows.limit: per-collector-plane outcome (COMPLETE / PARTIAL / FAILED, as the estate report calls them) has no metric: a plane that stopped collecting is visible only through stale evidence
rows.closes_with: a labelled counter per plane outcome, emitted by the discovery path

rows.question: can an operator see a queue that is not draining, or work that was given up on?
rows.note: added this pass: queued age, retry backlog, dead letters and worker leases, read from the same Redis keys the consumer uses
rows.limit: the retry/dead-letter/worker series are only emitted when REDIS_URL is set; without Redis the queue is in-process and unobservable by design
rows.closes_with: nothing further for a Redis deployment; in-memory mode is a dev path

rows.question: can an operator see that the database is unhealthy before users report it?
rows.note: reachability, per-dependency latency and an aggregate degraded flag
rows.limit: no connection-pool saturation metric (checked-out / overflow / waiting); a pool that is exhausted shows up as latency, not as pool pressure
rows.closes_with: emit SQLAlchemy pool status (checkedout, overflow, timeout count)

rows.question: can an operator see the evidence store going stale under a BOM?
rows.note: added this pass: evidence volume, stale evidence and current facts, so 'the BOM stopped changing' can be told apart from 'nothing was observed'
rows.limit: no chain-verification metric: evidence integrity is proven on demand (guide 112), not continuously monitored
rows.closes_with: a periodic verification job that emits its own age and verdict

rows.question: can an operator see that an agent on a host stopped reporting?

found.meaning: reporting counts agents inside AGENT_STALE_SECONDS; the age gauge is the stalest check-in, because the outlier is what the operator needs

rows.note: added this pass: the agent fleet was already recorded — heartbeats, status, buffered events — but nothing exposed it as a metric
rows.limit: the gauge is fleet-wide with no per-agent label: an operator learns that an agent is stale, then has to look up which one
rows.closes_with: a labelled series per agent (bounded by the enrolment count)

rows.question: can an operator see which planes stopped being covered?

found.reported_when: only after an estate discovery has been stored — with no run there is no coverage to report, which is correct: 'never observed' is not 'fully covered'

rows.note: added this pass: the last discovery's coverage matrix is emitted as one labelled series per plane plus a count of planes that are not fully covered, so a dark plane is an alert and not a screen
rows.limit: the read is platform-wide (metrics have no tenant context); in a multi-tenant deployment the gauges aggregate every tenant
rows.closes_with: tenant-labelled coverage series once a tenant-scoped scrape exists

rows.question: do the probes answer, and do they distinguish liveness from readiness?

worker_probe_q.detail: work waiting beyond threshold with no drain observed in the last hour

worker_probe_draining.detail: drain observed: 1 completion(s) in the last hour

found.meaning: three probes, three questions: liveness is the process, readiness is its dependencies, and the worker probe is whether anything is consuming — measured from the job and lease records, so it answers while the console is unreachable

rows.note: added this pass: /healthz/workers — the worker probe the console had, reachable by an orchestrator without a session, answering 503 only when work is waiting and nothing is draining
rows.limit: the probe reads the durable job and lease records, so it reports what the queue has done, not what a worker process is doing this second
rows.closes_with: a lease heartbeat on the queue consumer, carried into the same probe
rows.measured: liveness 200, readiness 200, worker probe 503 when stalled and 200 when draining

rows.question: is a single request traceable across API, worker and database?

otlp_export.meaning: the span a request finished is the span the collector received, with the same trace and span ids, the route as an attribute and the service name in the resource — export is off the request path and absent when unconfigured

rows.note: added this pass: the span exporter that already existed is executed — a real HTTP sink receives the OTLP/JSON of a finished span, with the same trace and span ids and the route as an attribute
rows.limit: the worker carries the trace id in its log context but does not open a child span, so a job's work is correlated by id rather than drawn as a trace; and no APM backend in this repository was sent the payload
rows.closes_with: a job-id span link opened by the consumer, and a collector the bank already runs
rows.measured: 1 OTLP notification(s) received, trace id matched, 623 bytes, exporter absent when unconfigured

rows.question: are logs structured, correlated and safe to ship?
rows.note: JSON logs through a shared logger, with request ids and redaction helpers
rows.limit: no shipping pipeline in this repository: whether logs reach the bank's SIEM is a deployment question
rows.closes_with: a documented log pipeline in the deployment guide

rows.question: does every alert reference a metric that exists, and is anything paging?

found.why_not_emitted: queue series need REDIS_URL and worker leases; the run had no Redis, so they were declared but absent

prometheus_wiring.note: rules are mounted at /etc/prometheus/rules/alerts.yml; without an Alertmanager stanza they evaluate and go nowhere

pager_path.meaning: a rule that exists in alerts.yml was posted as an Alertmanager notification to the receiver its own config names, was accepted, and is now a scraped series — the alert evaluates outside the system it watches and the platform can prove it was told

rows.note: 15 rules across availability, backlog, freshness and integrity; every series a rule names is checked against the endpoint's live output and the module's declared names, so a renamed metric fails this report instead of the pager — and added this pass, a rule from alerts.yml is delivered to the receiver alertmanager.yml names and counted in /metrics
rows.limit: no Prometheus scraped these rules and no Alertmanager process ran: the evaluation and the grouping are the bank's, and what is proven here is the delivery half — the receiver, the token and the counted series
rows.closes_with: nothing further in code; a bank points alertmanager.yml at its own pager and the same series proves delivery
rows.measured: 15 rules, 3 metrics referenced, receiver answered 200 with 1 alert(s) counted

limits: The metrics were served in-process against a scratch database seeded with one row of each kind. A populated estate changes the values, not the presence or the meaning of a series.

No Prometheus and no Alertmanager process ran here. The rules were checked against the endpoint's own output and a notification was delivered to the receiver the bundled config names; the evaluation interval, the grouping and the retry behaviour are Prometheus's, and unproven by this drill.
The span exporter was watched against a local HTTP sink, not an APM backend: the payload is OTLP/JSON and its ids are checked, but no vendor collector accepted it.

The worker probe reads durable job and lease records. A worker that is alive and idle looks the same as one that never started, which is why the probe reports 'Not measured' rather than inventing a state.
Log shipping to a SIEM is a deployment question and is graded READ: the structured logger and the redaction helpers exist, and this checkout cannot show what leaves the host.
